3'

  • N: ana pī ... [ ... ] ... ušamṣi ... [ ... ]
  • T: “I did as much as I needed … […].
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; pī ← pû I “(also OB)”; ušamṣi ← maṣû I “to correspond, comply with (s.th.)”
  • Note: [RN303: 114f.] suggests a-na pi₂-i l[i-bi?-i]a “Secondo il mio desiderio”. [Kienast_FS-Matouš: 184] restores a-na bi-i-t[u be-li₂-i]a u₂#-ša#-am-ṣi#-i-m[a nu-ni a-ba-ar] “Für den Tempel meines Herren hatte ich (gerade) genug | Fische [gefangen]”. [Dietrich_AOAT42: 43] and [RN1982: 254] restore a-na bi-i-t[u {d]e₂!#-a u₂-ša-am-ṣi-i-la#-[aš?-šu?]}, based on l. 60’.

4'

  • N: šūtu [ ... ] ... ahhīki mala i[baššû]
  • T: “O South Wind, […] your brothers, as m[any as there be],
  • L: šūtu ← šūtu II “south, south wind Bab., NA”; ahhīki ← ahu I “brother (st. constr. ahi, OA ahu/ū”; mala ← mala I “as much as”; i[baššû] ← bašû I “to be (at hand, available)”
  • Note: [Dietrich_AOAT42: 43] and [Kienast_FS-Matouš: 184], following [RN552: 430], read: [šu-um-hi]-ra-ni ah-he-e-ki ma-la i-[ba-aš-šu-u₂] “call up your brothers against me, as many as there are”. von Soden in turn refers to [Böhl.WdO2: 423 fn. 3], who restores the line in much the same fashion and to the same effect (“ruf die Brüder zu Hilfe”), only employing the (grammatically impossible) form pu-hu-ra-ni instead of šu-um-hi-ra-ni. [RN493: 16] suggests instead [ša?-a?]-ra-ni “the winds”.
AmaMB1 o 4'. šu-u₂-tu • [x x (x)]-ra-ni •* ah-he-e-ki • ma-la i-[ba-aš-šu-u₂ (•)]

5'

  • N: ka[ppa]ki lū šebir
  • T: “Let your wi[ng] be fractured!”
  • L: ka[ppa]ki ← kappu I “wing O/jB of bird, ant, god, statue”; lū ← lū I “let it be”; šebir ← šebēru I “to break”
  • Note: Many of the previous editors of Adapa understand the verb as lušebbir “I will break”. However, as the verb occurs in the G stem elsewhere in this composition (l. 12’, l. 49’) when a transitive meaning is implied, the form is here taken as a precative stative “it shall be broken”. This is also how [Dietrich_AOAT42: 43] and [RN1982: 254] understand the form.
  • Parallels: cf. (Adapa Sum. Meturan 65a)
AmaMB1 o 5'a. ka-a-[ap-pa]-ki [(•)] lu-u₂ še-bi-ir •

  • Parallels: cf. L I.7 SB "-" b+11; cf. (Adapa Sum. Meturan 111-112)

  • L: šup[ur-ma? ← šapāru I “to send”; li]lqûniššu? ← leqû II “to take, take over”; annikâ ← annikīam I “here, hither O/MB”

15'

  • N: ea ša šamê idī ilpus[s]ū-ma
  • T: Ea, he of heaven, touched his arms,
  • L: ea ← Ea I; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; šamê ← šamû I “mostly pl. tant. sky, heaven”; idī ← idu I “pl. m. & f. arm”; ilpus[s]ū-ma ← lapātu I “to touch, take hold of”
  • Note: i-di is here taken to be an obl. dl. form of idu “side, arm” in accordance with the interpretation brought forward by [RN552: 431], who translates “Hier berührte der ‘Ea des Himmels’ [ihm] die Arme”. Most other editors of the text understand it as a form of idû “to know”. To circumvent the problem of the missing subjunctive ending, [RN216: 185], [Dietrich_AOAT42: 46] and [RN303: 117] interpret ša šamê as “the things/ways of heaven” and translate the whole phrase as a parenthesis. [RN164: 527] also seems to follow their interpretation (“the ways of heaven”), yet still chooses to translate the phrase (more freely) as a relative clause.
  • Parallels: cf. (Adapa Sum. Meturan 136-136a)
AmaMB1 o 14'b. {d}e₂-a ša ša-me-e i-di • il-pu-us-[s]u₂?-ma# [(•)]

  • N: ammīni ea amīlūta lā banīta ša šamê u erṣeti ukellinši
  • T: “Why did Ea disclose to a reprehensible human being something of heaven and earth,
  • L: ammīni ← ammīni I “why?”; ea ← Ea I; amīlūta ← awīlūtu I “humanity”; lā ← lā I “not, no”; banīta ← banû I “good, beautiful of person, animal”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; šamê ← šamû I “mostly pl. tant. sky, heaven”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; erṣeti ← erṣetu I “earth, land”; ukellinši ← kullumu I
  • Note: The sign sequence LA.BA.NI.TA has been parsed by most scholars as lā banīta “not good”, which is also followed here. The suggestion lā balitta, brought forward by [Bing_JANES18: 2], cannot be maintained for reasons of graphic conventions, see [RN493: 29]. Perhaps one could also consider reading la ma!-ni-ta (lā manīta), which would yield “Why did Ea disclose to humanity (such) countless amount(s) (of knowledge) about heaven and earth?”. On the question whether to understand the adjective as an attribute of amīlūta “human(ity)” or, nominalised, as the object of disclosure, see [RN493: 28f.] with earlier literature.

75'

  • N: lā balṭāta ai nišī ... [ ... ] ...
  • T: “Won’t you live? Alas for the […] peoples!”
  • L: lā ← lā I “not, no”; balṭāta ← balāṭu II “to live”; ai ← ai II “alas! Bab.”; nišī ← nišu I “mostly pl. nišū”
  • Note: One possible restoration is da-a-l[a?-t]i, that is a f. pl. form of dallu “small, inferior”. It is favoured by Izreel ([RN493: 20; 32] and [RN24a: 44-46, 49f.] “inferior”, [Izreel_GS-Kutscher: 54f., 57] “poor”) as well as [RN216: 187] (“downtrodden”), [RN164: 529] (“wretched”), [RN1982: 258f.] (“kümmerlich”) and [RN2168: 60] (“poor”). [RN493: 32] bases his reading the transliteration given by [RN1743a: 968], who apparently saw a half broken LA, whereas none of the copies of the tablet feature the sign. Anothere possibility is to restore da-a-[ša-t]i, i.e. a form of dēšû “flourishing”, as does von [RN552: 431] (“sich mehrend”). A less likely suggestion is given by [Böhl.WdO2: 426]: He reads the passage as ai irši ṭāti “dafür habe er [...] kein Bestechungsgeschenk”, which he takes as an idiomatic expression to the effect of “Das steht unabänderlich fest”.
